title: Jake Castillo: UGC creator playbook that took Cal AI to 15M users (zero to $10K/month)
summary: Jake Castillo, former CMO of Cal AI, lays out a five-step UGC creator system for taking an app from zero to $10K/month: source talking-head creators, warm up dedicated accounts, pick a content format (magic moment vs painful problem), run RPM vs CPM economics, then cut and scale creators. Includes concrete pricing, benchmarks and ratios.

principles.text: Good outputs start with great inputs; creators are your inputs, and weak on-camera talent breaks the whole system.
principles.quote: good outputs start with great inputs and creators are your inputs. You can have the best scripts and the best app in the world, but if the person delivering the content isn't compelling, it's impossible to make the system work.

principles.text: Small teams should use UGC creators on brand-new dedicated accounts instead of paying expensive large influencers.
principles.quote: For a small startup or solo founder, paying large influencers can get very expensive. That's why I really like UGC.

principles.text: Test creators cheaply first (10 videos at $10), then move proven ones to a full campaign with view bonuses.
principles.quote: I'm talking like 10 test videos at $10 a video. And if those videos are good, then you can extend them to like a full campaign where it's 30 videos a month at $30 per video

principles.text: Warm up creator accounts and prove they aren't shadowbanned before posting branded content.
principles.quote: And then once you see a video breaks a thousand views, you can have them start posting actual branded content.

principles.text: Pick content format by asking: magic moment means maximize views; else a painful problem means maximize intent; else rethink the product.
principles.quote: The first question you got to ask is does my app have a magic moment? And by magic moment, I mean a feature that is so visually impressive that if someone sees it on screen, they're going to do almost like a double take.

principles.text: Judge creators by revenue per 1,000 views against what you paid per 1,000 views, and scale when RPM clearly beats CPM.
principles.quote: if I'm paying a $1.50 to acquire a customer that pays me $4, then I'm ready to scale.
